chunks: And it is narrated from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I came to Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام with a bondwoman, offering her to him. He began bargaining with me and I bargained with him; then I sold her to him, and he finalized it through my hand. So I said, “May I be your ransom, I only bargained with you to see whether bargaining is proper or not proper,” and I said, “I have reduced ten dinars from your price.”
He said, “Far from it! Why was this not before the finalization? Has the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله not reached you: ‘A price reduction after finalization is forbidden’?”

key_terms.الضَّمَّةِ: the point of finalization or conclusion of the transaction
key_terms.الْوَضِيعَةُ: a reduction in the agreed price
key_terms.فَضَمِنَ: he finalized and assumed the sale
key_terms.يُسَاوِمُنِي: he bargained with me over the sale price

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to reduce the agreed sale price after a transaction has already been finalized in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling in sales: once the transaction has been concluded and finalized, reducing the agreed price afterward is not permitted. It also shows Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام invoking the prophetic tradition as the basis for the ruling.
